title: Should Investors Buy AT&T Stock Instead of Verizon Stock? | T Stock Analysis | VZ Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; captions readable
summary: Parkevtate compares the two telecom dividend stocks head-to-head for passive-income investors and ranks both BUY: T at $25 (stated, DCF fair value $34.60, 4.4% yield) and VZ at $47 (stated, DCF fair value $55, 5.9% yield). His advice: split a purchase 50/50 between the two, but if forced to pick only one, AT&T has the slight edge as the more undervalued. The analysis: both grow revenue at low single digits in a saturated market; operating margins are improving (AT&T 17%→21%, Verizon 21%→22.7%) partly on AI productivity gains; but neither allocates capital well — AT&T's ROIC is 8.11% (about its WACC) and Verizon's has slid from ~12% to ~6% (below WACC), which matters because the looming 6G upgrade cycle will demand tens of billions in capex. Both trade at a deserved discount to the S&P 500 (AT&T 9.9x forward PE, Verizon 8.9x), though he finds the discount overdone versus his DCF values. He also warns dividend investors that a 5.9% yield beats long bonds only if the share price at least holds flat — price declines can wipe out the yield. The video is sponsored by The Motley Fool. No stance flips (T reaffirms his 28 Sep BUY; first recorded call on VZ).

calls.thesis: Ranked BUY with 4.4% yield; DCF fair value $34.60 vs $25 market price; if forced to pick one, AT&T is the better stock (he suggests a 50/50 split of the two otherwise).
calls.bull_case: Low-single-digit organic revenue growth, op margins up to 21%, 4.4% yield.
calls.bear_case: Saturated market; ROIC 8.11% and never above 12% in a decade; massive 5G->6G capex cycles.
